title: Font Rendering: FOUT vs FOIT, font-display, and Metric Overrides

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a web page needs a special font, it has two choices while downloading it: hide the text completely until the fancy font arrives (leaving invisible ghost text, called FOIT), or show a standard system font right away and swap it later (FOUT). `font-display` lets you choose between invisible text and instant reading.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT) happens when the browser hides text while downloading a web font (default `font-display: block` with a 3-second invisible timeout). Flash of Unstyled Text (FOUT) happens when the browser immediately renders a fallback system font and swaps to the custom font once loaded (`font-display: swap`). Use `font-display: optional` for the fastest performance without layout shifts.
progressiveExplaining.senior: The CSS font-display timeline comprises three phases: **Block Period** (invisible fallback), **Swap Period** (fallback displayed, swapped upon custom font arrival), and **Failure Period** (custom font treated as failed). While `swap` fixes FOIT and improves LCP, it introduces Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) during the swap. Modern font optimization uses CSS font metric overrides (`size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, `line-gap-override`) to morph the fallback font's bounding boxes to match the target web font.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: The text shaping engine (e.g. HarfBuzz in Blink) measures glyph advance widths and line-height bounding metrics. With `font-display: swap`, when the `.woff2` font completes decoding, the layout engine triggers a targeted style and layout invalidation, re-shaping and re-flowing text nodes. When `size-adjust` is applied, the engine scales the glyph coordinate system of the fallback `@font-face` at layout time, preventing reflow displacement.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `font-display: swap` and `font-display: optional`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your precision regarding Core Web Vitals optimization and low-network conditions.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `font-display: swap` gives a 0ms block period and an infinite swap period: the fallback font renders immediately and will *always* swap when the web font downloads (even if it takes 10 seconds). `font-display: optional` gives a tiny 100ms block period and a **0ms swap period**: if the web font is already in cache, it uses it; if not, it uses the fallback font for the entire life of the page and caches the web font for subsequent page loads, guaranteeing **zero layout shift**.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `font-display: optional` can result in the web font not displaying on the first visit if the network roundtrip exceeds ~100ms.

interviewGotchas.question: How do `size-adjust` and `ascent-override` prevent Cumulative Layout Shift?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: This tests knowledge of CSS font metric calculations.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Fallback fonts (e.g. Arial) and custom web fonts (e.g. Inter) possess different bounding boxes and character advance widths. When `font-display: swap` swaps the font, the line height and paragraph wrapping change, shifting elements below it (causing CLS). `size-adjust` scales the fallback font's glyph glyphs proportionally, and `ascent-override` / `descent-override` match the exact vertical line heights, making the fallback occupy the exact same pixel dimensions as the custom font.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Metric overrides must be applied to the *fallback* `@font-face` definition (using `src: local(...)`), not to the custom font definition itself.
